kind.text:
Ran 2026-08-17: the file asserts the NEGATION of formal.statement and the harness printed `; evidence kind=unsat-quant-instance-set certified=1 recheck=na arena=ok ms=22`, then `unsat`. This fact was `open` until this date and this row is what closed it; the reason it was open is recorded in the fact's notes and is worth reading, because the gap was never the theorem.

WHAT THE CERTIFICATE IS. `Evidence::UnsatQuantInstanceSet`, a `QuantifierInstanceSetCertificate` (`crates/axeyum-solver/src/quant_instance_set_cert.rs`). It contains no term of the producing run at all: a per-assertion count of top-level existential binders eliminated (here `[1]`), and one universal instantiation naming its universal by INDEX into the skolemised assertion list and its single binding as `Witness { assertion: 0, index: 0 }` -- 'the witness introduced for the outermost existential of assertion 0'. Positional, because a `TermId` from the producing arena names nothing in a checker's.

WHAT `arena=ok` MEANS HERE. `Evidence::check` re-parsed the file into an arena sharing nothing with the solve and then, in that arena: re-ran the SAME existential elimination (`auto::eliminate_top_existentials`) to obtain ITS OWN witness -- so freshness, the soundness condition for eliminating an existential, is established by the checker rather than taken from the producer; required the recorded binder counts to equal its own; rebuilt the instance by substituting its own witness into its own universal; replayed that instance through the public `check_quantifier_ground_derivation`; rebuilt the ground set from its own non-universal assertions plus that instance (so nothing can be smuggled into a set the checker constructs); and re-refuted it.

WHAT IS NOT CERTIFIED, stated because the route name could otherwise flatter it. The final sufficiency step re-invokes `auto::check_auto` on the ground residue rather than checking a clause-level proof object. Measured 2026-08-17 with `cargo run --release -q -p axeyum-bench --example diagnose_evidence` on that residue (`(= (shaves sk sk) (not (shaves sk sk)))`): `euf-online: decided unsat`. So the CDCL(T) EUF core and its CNF abstraction are in the trust base, and -- unlike the other `smt-clausal` facts in this ledger -- there is NO DRAT or Alethe object here. What this certificate independently establishes is the QUANTIFIER reduction: the existential elimination and the one instantiation that were previously performed, recorded, and then dropped on the floor.

Independently cross-checked: `z3 -smt2` (/usr/bin/z3) on the same file also reports `unsat`.

kind.text:
CLOSED 2026-08-17 by the `skolem-cert` lane. This fact was `open` for three days for exactly one reason -- the right verdict with no checkable object -- and the whole history of that gap is kept below, unedited, because it is the more useful half of the record. What changed: nothing about the solver's ANSWER, and nothing about the reconstruction path this fact's earlier notes describe. The instantiation the RECONSTRUCTION TRACE below says was 'performed, recorded, and never plumbed out' is now plumbed out, as an `Evidence::UnsatQuantInstanceSet`, and the certificate records the existential elimination POSITIONALLY (how many binders each assertion lost) rather than by `TermId`, which is what lets a checker redo the elimination in its own arena and land on its own witness. Two earlier designs that recorded the skolemised terms or trusted the ids to line up are described in `crates/axeyum-solver/src/quant_instance_set_cert.rs`; both failed, one by aborting and one by reporting `certified=1` on a check that said FAIL.

The evidence row's `notes` state precisely what the certificate does and does not establish -- in particular that the final ground refutation is delegated back to `check_auto` (measured: the online EUF/CDCL(T) route), so this fact is on `smt-clausal` with the SAT core in its footprint and carries no DRAT or Alethe object. What is independently re-derived is the QUANTIFIER reduction.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GATE: this instance was the negative control of `scripts/check-smt-evidence-certified.py`, and that check FAILED ON PURPOSE the moment the certificate landed, with the message it was written to emit. The control has been repointed at `artifacts/facts/smt2/neg-no-integer-square-is-minus-one.smt2` (`F:no-integer-square-is-minus-one`, open), and this instance is now SWEPT by that check as a settled one, where it must keep reporting `certified=1`.

--- THE RECORD FROM WHEN THIS WAS OPEN, VERBATIM ---

OPEN IN THIS LEDGER, NOT IN MATHEMATICS. axeyum gets the right VERDICT and no usable evidence, which is a more interesting failure than returning `unknown`. Measured 2026-08-14 with `cargo run -q -p axeyum-bench --example smtcomp_cli -- --evidence artifacts/facts/smt2/neg-barber-no-such-barber.smt2`: it printed `; evidence kind=unsat-drat certified=0 recheck=na arena=FAIL ms=171` and then `unsat`. Read that line carefully, because two of its fields WERE misreported by the harness rather than by the solver -- both are now fixed; see the 2026-08-17 update at the end. The evidence object is a BARE `Evidence::Unsat(None)` -- no certificate at all -- but `Evidence::kind_label` maps every `Unsat` variant to the string `unsat-drat`, so the line names a DRAT proof that does not exist; and `Evidence::check` returns `Ok(false)` for a bare unsat, which the CLI renders as `arena=FAIL`, i.e. as though a certificate had been examined and found wanting. `Evidence::check_outcome` on the same input correctly answers `NothingToCheck(UncertifiedUnsat)`. The verdict is right, the certificate is absent, and the status here stays `open` because an uncertified unsat is not evidence under this schema. The proposition is one universal instantiation (x := b) away from the already-proved F:no-self-negating-proposition. [CORRECTED 2026-08-17: the second half of this sentence previously read `but that instantiation step is one no component of ours performed or recorded`, and that is FALSE -- see the reconstruction trace in the update below.] UPDATE 2026-08-17: the two harness misreports above are REPAIRED, re-measured with the same command: it now prints `; evidence kind=unsat-uncertified certified=0 recheck=na arena=none:uncertified-unsat`. `Evidence::kind_label` now distinguishes the variants (`crates/axeyum-solver/src/evidence.rs:725-726`: `Unsat(Some(_)) => "unsat-drat"`, `Unsat(None) => "unsat-uncertified"`), so the line no longer names a DRAT proof that does not exist, and `arena=FAIL` -- which read as though a certificate had been examined and rejected -- is now `arena=none:uncertified-unsat`, which says there was nothing to examine. The SUBSTANCE is unchanged: right verdict, no certificate, status stays `open`. What changed on this date is that the gap is now GATED rather than merely recorded. `scripts/check-smt-evidence-certified.py` requires every settled smt-term-level / smt-clausal fact to report `certified=1` (measured: 17 of 17 do), because the evidence commands those facts carry test only the VERDICT -- `test "$(... | tail -1)" = unsat` passes on an uncertified refutation, verified against this very instance. This instance is that check's negative control: genuinely unsat so a verdict-only checker accepts it, genuinely uncertified so a certification-aware one must not. If it ever reports `certified=1` the check FAILS on purpose, saying that this fact can now be closed and the control must be repointed. RECONSTRUCTION TRACE 2026-08-17 (measured, `AXEYUM_QTRACE=1`): the solver DOES perform and DOES record the instantiation. `auto::solve` skolemizes the top existential to `!sk_0`, then the e-graph route (`prove_quantified_unsat_via_egraph`) admits exactly one instance -- the universal at the existential's own Skolem witness -- and `check_auto` refutes the resulting `p = not p`. That instance is recorded as a `QuantifierInstanceCertificate` (`crates/axeyum-solver/src/qinst_egraph.rs:2737`) which already has a PUBLIC independent checker, `check_quantifier_ground_derivation` (:2821). It is simply never plumbed out: the certificates live in a function-local `ground_derivations` map (:1162) that dies at each `return Ok(Unsat)`, `skolemize_top_existentials` (`auto.rs:889`) returns `Vec<TermId>` and discards the assertion-to-`!sk_k` correspondence, and `evidence.rs` references neither (grep: 0 hits). `prove_unsat_to_lean` declines at `skolem_alethe.rs:102-105`, whose slice requires the existential's body to be a single quantifier-free equality; the barber's body is a universal, so both conjuncts fail. So this is NOT a proposition whose refutation is unreconstructable -- it is one where the reconstruction path re-derives the instantiation from scratch with a strictly weaker vocabulary (witness search reads only the ground partition, and `b` occurs only under the binder) and a strictly weaker ground gate (congruence-only, needing exactly one disequality, which `p = not p` does not have). Measured control: the fully instantiated ground formula `(= (shaves b b) (not (shaves b b)))` DOES reconstruct kernel-checked today. Only the instantiation step is missing.
